processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting and casting into cylindrical copper moulds
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Moulds 32 mm diameter × 186 mm length; no further heat treatment reported (as-cast terminal state).

processing_steps.method: spark erosion cutting and surface grinding
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Mechanical test specimens were cut from cast ingots by spark erosion in the direction of the longitudinal axis of the ingot (casting direction); specimen surfaces were ground.

structures.overall_structure: Fe3Al matrix with TaC precipitates (cube-like, script-like)

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression samples (6×6×10) mm³; tensile flat samples (3.5×5) mm² cross-section with 15 mm gauge length

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering compression stress-strain curve (curve 12 in Fig. 2b) for Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C shows nearly constant hardening rate over long strain intervals, in the group of carbide-forming alloys that harden at nearly constant rate.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Yield stress in compression/tension vs binary Fe-26Al reference; at elevated temperatures all Fe-Al-M-C alloys show strengthening effects relative to the corresponding binary reference alloys.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: load 62.5 g, indentation ball 2.5 mm diameter
characterization_methods.purpose: Provide preliminary information on mechanical properties of the matrix.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: deformation rate 10^-4 s^-1; elevated-temperature tests in protective argon atmosphere within a radiation furnace; specimens held 30 min at testing temperature before loading; temperature checked by NiCr-Ni thermocouple on specimen surface
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine yield stress in compression/tension, ductility, and hardening behaviour at room and elevated temperatures.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C: room-temperature compressive yield stress 594 MPa; tensile yield stress and total elongation not determined ('-'); brittle behaviour with IGD+TGC fracture.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM-Hitachi S-530, 20 kV, working distance 15 mm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: secondary electrons (SE), 10 μm scale bar in fractographs
characterization_methods.purpose: Investigate fracture surfaces of ruptured tensile specimens.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C fracture surface is partially intergranular (smooth) and partially transgranular (facetted), corresponding to IGD+TGC.

unmapped_findings: Room-temperature tensile yield stress and total elongation for Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C are reported as '-' (not determined) in Table 2, so no tensile strength/ductility values are available for this as-cast sample.

Fracture mode of Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C at room temperature is IGD+TGC (intergranular decohesion + transgranular cleavage); the SEM fractograph (Fig. 4l) shows partially intergranular (smooth) and partially transgranular (facetted) fracture.

In elevated-temperature compression tests, Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C (like other Nb/Ta-containing Fe-26Al alloys) shows its yield-stress-anomaly peak shifted towards lower temperatures and higher stresses compared with binary Fe-26Al; no numeric peak temperature/stress is reported for this specific alloy.

At 650 °C and 800 °C, the compressive yield stress of Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C exceeds its tensile yield stress, consistent with the tension-compression asymmetry reported for all investigated alloys (Figs. 7 and 8).
Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C is one of the Nb/Ta-containing alloys reported to show the highest strengthening effects at room temperature and at elevated temperatures relative to other Fe-Al-M-C alloys.
